papers.title_in_file: Harnessing Quantum Dynamics for Robust and Scalable Quantum Extreme Learning Machines
papers.what_it_is: A Deloitte study that simulates Quantum Extreme Learning Machine embeddings on classical hardware with MPS and TDVP tensor network methods, tested on MNIST.

assertions.value: The authors report that approximate embeddings from the TDVP one-site tensor network method give classification accuracy that matches a nonlinear neural network on classical features, within the margin of error.
quotes: Importantly, the accuracy achieved by the QELM embedding using the TDVP one site method matches that of the nonlinear NN model with classical features, within the margin of error.
even approximate embeddings generated by scalable TN algorithms yield classification accuracies comparable to those of nonlinear classical models, including neural networks (NNs).
assertions.certainty_reason: One simulated study on one dataset; the figures are in Fig. 9, not quoted.
assertions.reader_inference: The result concerns classical simulation of a quantum-inspired model, so it bears on whether quantum hardware is needed.

assertions.value: The authors report that some entanglement is needed to enrich the feature space, while excessive entanglement causes feature concentration and lower model performance.
quotes: while some entanglement is necessary to enrich the feature space, excessive entanglement can result in feature concentration and diminished model performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from the authors' own simulations.

assertions.value: The authors state that their numerical experiments use the MNIST dataset with an MPS-based QELM for classification, and that applying the algorithm to more complex datasets is future work.
quotes: we performed numerical experiments using the MNIST [52] dataset using our MPS-based QELM for classification.
Looking ahead, it will be important to explore how this algorithm can be applied to more complex or
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own dataset and says broader datasets are untested (Conclusion and Outlook).

papers.partial_detail: Preface, Section 2 start (VQE, ansatz), Section 5.2.1 barren plateaus, Conclusion; other sections skimmed via table of contents
papers.what_it_is: A single-author tutorial (blogposts collected as a PDF) on VQE, QAOA and variational quantum algorithms.

assertions.value: The author states that, as of February 2024, there is an increasing consensus in the community that using VQAs on NISQ devices for practical purposes faces fundamental issues.
quotes: But by now (February 2024), there is an increasing consensus in the community that using VQAs on NISQ devices for any practical purposes faces fundamental issues
assertions.certainty_reason: The author's own impression of community opinion, no survey or data given.

assertions.value: The author states, describing the work of McClean and colleagues, that for random quantum circuits the gradient is small in most places and the chance that it is arbitrarily close to zero at a random point grows exponentially with the number of qubits and parameters.
quotes: In 2018 Jarrod McClean et al. pointed out that there are two big problems with training variational quantum circuits.
And the chance that it's arbitrarily close to zero for a random point grows exponentially with the number of qubits and number of parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the document attributes to McClean et al.

assertions.value: The author states that VQE finds an upper bound of the lowest eigenvalue of a given Hamiltonian.
quotes: VQE allows us to find an upper bound of the lowest eigenvalue of a given Hamiltonian.
assertions.certainty_reason: The author's definition of VQE in Section 2.1.1.

assertions.value: The author states that the document is aimed at readers with a basic understanding of quantum computing concepts and linear algebra, and that intuitive explanations are preferred over mathematical rigor.
quotes: This document is targeted at people with a basic understanding of quantum computing concepts and linear algebra.
I personally prefer that over mathematical rigor
assertions.certainty_reason: The preface states the audience and the rigor trade-off.

papers.title_in_file: Unlocking Quantum Optimization: A Use Case Study on NISQ Systems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 6 Conclusion; experimental sections not read in detail
papers.what_it_is: A Fraunhofer IAO study that runs QAOA, VQE and quantum annealing on IBM and D-Wave hardware for two industrial optimization use cases.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the IBM quantum systems only small proof-of-concept examples can be executed with acceptable quality, and that solution quality deteriorates quickly for larger instances with a lack of reproducibility and predictability.
quotes: In particular, we observe that on the IBM quantum systems only small proof-of-concept examples can be executed with an acceptable quality.
For larger problem instances the solution quality quickly deteriorates and throughout all examples we find a lack of reproducibility and predictability.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from the authors' own hardware runs on two use cases.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the D-Wave annealer larger instances could be run, but solution quality decreases with problem size, which they call a clear limit to usability for industry relevant problems.
quotes: Nevertheless, again the solution quality decreases with the problem size which poses a clear limit to the usability also of quantum annealers for industry relevant problems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from the authors' own runs.

assertions.value: The authors report that comparing different generations of IBM quantum processors, result quality improved with the evolution of the hardware.
quotes: comparing the different generations of IBM quantum processors we could clearly observe the improvement of the result quality with the evolution of the hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison across processor generations.

assertions.value: The authors state that they study two industrial use cases, electric vehicle charging schedules and truck routes, run on IBM gate-based processors and a D-Wave quantum annealer.
quotes: This paper addresses precisely this gap by considering two industrial relevant use cases: one in the realm of optimizing charging schedules for electric vehicles, the other concerned with the optimization of truck routes.
execute on different processors of the gate-based quantum computers of IBM as well as on the quantum annealer of D-Wave
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the paper's own setup and scope.

papers.title_in_file: Kernel-based dequantization of variational QML without Random Fourier Features
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 7 Conclusions; derivations in Sections 3 to 6 not checked step by step
papers.what_it_is: A short theory note showing that certain PQC-inspired kernels, with reweightings from symmetric MPS, can be evaluated exactly and efficiently classically.

assertions.value: The authors show that a class of reweighted PQC-inspired kernels, with reweightings induced from symmetric matrix product states, can be evaluated exactly and efficiently classically, without Random Fourier Features.
quotes: we show that the kernels whose evaluation is approximated by RFF in this dequantization algorithm can in fact often be evaluated exactly and efficiently classically.
In this work, we have shown that the class of reweighted PQC-inspired kernels, with reweightings induced from symmetric MPS, can in fact be evaluated exactly and efficiently classically.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived in Section 4 (exact and efficient evaluation of kernels with MPS-induced reweightings); summarized in Section 7. I did not check the proof steps.
assertions.reader_inference: Narrows the set of regression settings where variational QML could keep an edge over classical methods.

assertions.value: The authors state that the conditions from prior work also imply settings in which kernel based dequantization cannot be efficient, and name learning parities as an explicit example.
quotes: We stress that the conditions from [SRJ+23] also imply the existence of settings in which kernel based dequantization cannot be efficient.
One can indeed construct an explicit example of such a setting by considering the problem of learning parities
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors attribute this to prior work, not to their own proof.

assertions.value: The authors state that their note covers a wide range of instances and that the approach is for regression problems, not a general dequantization of variational QML.
quotes: In this short note we show that for a wide range of instances, this approach can be simplified.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the scope of the note.

papers.title_in_file: Bayesian autotuning of Hubbard model quantum simulators
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction start, Section VII Conclusions; methods and results sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A study that uses SVM and Bayesian optimization to find gate voltages in quantum dot arrays that realize a target Hubbard model.

assertions.value: The authors report that they predicted the voltages needed to prepare a double quantum dot Hubbard model within 1.5% error for model gates and 6% error for experimental gates.
quotes: We were able to predict voltages needed in experiment to prepare on demand double QD Hubbard model within 1.5% error for model gates and 6% error for experimental gates.
assertions.certainty_reason: Computed from gate lithography images and calculated integrals, one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the SVM classified potential profiles by suitability for the tight-binding approximation, reducing the voltage search space by 99%.
quotes: Using SVM we classified potential profiles based on suitability for tight-binding approximation reducing the space by 99%.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study's classifier result.

assertions.value: The authors report an accuracy of 10% for both tunnelling parameters in larger arrays, within the same number of iterations as for the two-dot system.
quotes: We reach an accuracy of 10% for both tunnelling parameters t within the same number of iterations as used for two-QD system.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study's result for a three-dot array.

assertions.value: The authors state that their results rely on accurate experimental gate images and realistic integrals from linear combinations of harmonic orbitals calculations.
quotes: Our results rely on accurate experimental gate images and realistic integrals based on LCHO calculation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The conclusion states the inputs the results depend on.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Positional Encodings for Graph Neural Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 4 propositions (statements only), Section 5, Section 6; appendix proofs not read
papers.what_it_is: A Pasqal ICML 2024 paper proposing positional encodings for graph neural networks computed from quantum system observables.

assertions.value: The authors state that they prove some positional encodings using quantum features are theoretically more expressive than ones based on random walk and Laplacian eigenvectors, on strongly regular graphs.
quotes: We prove that some of these quantum features are theoretically more expressive for certain graphs than the commonly used relative random walk probabilities.
We proved that some positional encodings that use quantum features are theoretically more expressive than ones based on simple random walk and laplacian eigenvectors, on strongly regular graphs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Propositions 4.1 to 4.7 and Appendix B; the text also says the distinction for some cases is shown by experiment, so I could not tell which part is proved.

assertions.value: The authors report that on an artificial binary graph classification dataset the quantum encoding models reach 100% accuracy and the classical models reach 45% accuracy.
quotes: The quantum encoding models achieve 100% accuracy whereas all other classical models achieve 45% accuracy.
We were able to engineer an artificial dataset for which classical approaches fail to perform the associated binary classification tasks
assertions.certainty_reason: Dataset built by the authors to favor the quantum encoding.
assertions.reader_inference: The dataset was constructed to separate the methods, so it does not show an advantage on real data.

assertions.value: The authors report a small gain in performance over state-of-the-art models using quantum features that are efficiently computable.
quotes: we were able to show a small gain in performance compared to state-of-the-art models.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on benchmarks.

assertions.value: The authors state that it remains unclear whether an actual performance improvement will be observed on real-world use cases, and whether it will justify the cost of quantum hardware.
quotes: While it remains unclear whether an actual performance improvement will be observed on real-world use cases, and whether this improvement will justify the cost of using quantum hardware in the future
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 6 states the limit in the authors' own words.

papers.title_in_file: Comprehensive Survey of QML: From Data Analysis to Algorithmic Advancements
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction start, Section 7 Conclusion; body sections not read in full
papers.what_it_is: A survey of quantum machine learning algorithms, applications and challenges.

assertions.value: The authors state that, while the potential for exponential speedups is evident, the field faces significant challenges including hardware constraints, noise and limited qubit coherence in the NISQ era.
quotes: While the potential for exponential speedups and enhanced efficiency is evident, the field faces significant challenges, including hardware constraints, noise, and limited qubit coherence in the current era of Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey statement, no single study behind it.

assertions.value: The authors state that QML offers promising solutions that can significantly outperform classical approaches in specific scenarios.
quotes: QML offers promising solutions that can significantly outperform classical approaches in specific scenarios.
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion of a survey; no result is given with this statement.

assertions.value: The authors state that benchmarking quantum algorithms against classical counterparts will be crucial for identifying practical use cases where quantum advantages can be realized.
quotes: Benchmarking quantum algorithms against classical counterparts will be crucial for identifying practical use cases where quantum advantages can be realized.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statement about open work.

papers.title_in_file: Anomaly Detection with Quantum SVR in the NISQ Era: Limits of Robustness to Noise and Adversarial Attacks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 5 Conclusion; methods and result tables not read in detail
papers.what_it_is: A Fraunhofer AISEC benchmark of quantum support vector regression for anomaly detection on IBM hardware, with noise and adversarial attack tests.

assertions.value: The authors report that on 27-qubit IBM hardware the average AUC was slightly lower than the noiseless simulation (0.72 compared to 0.76), and that the QSVR outperformed the simulation on two of eleven datasets.
quotes: We first benchmarked our QSVR for semisupervised AD on 27-qubits IBM hardware and found that the average AUC was slightly lower than that of the noiseless simulation (0.72 compared to 0.76).
However, the QSVR outperformed the noiseless simulation on two out of eleven datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: One benchmark on eleven datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that the QSVR is largely robust against depolarizing, phase damping, phase flip and bit flip noise, while amplitude damping causes the most degradation and miscalibration noise also hurts performance.
quotes: revealing that it is largely robust against deporarizing, phasedamping, phase flip and bit flip noise.
Amplitude damping, on the other hand, results in the most significant degradation of the model and miscalibration noise also impacts performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated noise channels in one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the QSVR is highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks, and that quantum noise does not help robustness.
quotes: it was observed that the model is highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks.
Introducing quantum noise does not yield any beneficial effect, neither on the unattacked model's performance nor on its adversarial robustness.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study's adversarial experiments.
assertions.reader_inference: Bears on fraud and security use of quantum kernels: weak attacks already harm the model.

assertions.value: The authors state that they run a benchmark on IBM quantum hardware using eleven datasets.
quotes: by conducting a comprehensive benchmark on IBM quantum hardware using eleven datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the paper's own setup.
